question: For how many years are the non-permanent members of the UN Security Council (UNSC) elected?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) consists of 15 members.
 
• Among these, there are 5 permanent members: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
 
• The remaining 10 are non-permanent members who are elected by the General Assembly for a term of 2 years.
 
• Non-permanent members are elected based on regional groupings to ensure representation from different parts of the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Nations Security Council (UNSC)**

 
 
• The UNSC is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations, charged with ensuring international peace and security.
 
• It has the authority to establish peacekeeping operations, enact international sanctions, and authorize military action.
 
• Decisions on substantive matters require nine votes, including the concurring votes of all five permanent members, which means any of these can veto a decision.
 
 
 
• **Election of Non-Permanent Members**
 
 
• Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly of the United Nations.
 
• Each year, five non-permanent members are elected for a two-year term.
 
• To be elected, a country must receive at least two-thirds of the votes cast by the General Assembly members.
 
• These elections are based on regional distribution to ensure representation from various global regions.
 
 
 
• **Roles and Responsibilities**
 
 
• Non-permanent members participate in UNSC meetings and discussions, contributing to decisions and resolutions.
 
• They have the responsibility to uphold international peace and security.
 
• While they do not have veto power, their votes and participation are crucial in forming the council's decisions.
